### 1. Background

Customer operates a distributed system with OpenTelemetry-based
observability and a `[Playwright / Cypress]` test suite running in
`[CI system]`. Customer wishes to evaluate the open-source ARIP
(Autonomous Reliability Investigation Platform — Apache-2.0,
https://github.com/hamzayasaryilmaz/arip) as a potential addition
to their CI failure-investigation workflow.

This SOW covers a **two-week paid pilot** to assess fit, deliver
a working integration, and produce a telemetry hygiene audit
report.

### 2. Scope of work

Provider will:

1. **Telemetry audit (Week 1, Days 1–3).**
   Receive a 1-hour telemetry sample from Customer's
   `[Jaeger / Tempo / Elasticsearch / other]` backend. Run ARIP's
   prerequisite gate + hygiene findings + quality assessment.
   Produce a written report covering: distributed tracing
   readiness, span-tree gaps, service coverage, business-key
   propagation, log-source completeness, prioritized fix list.

2. **Integration build (Week 1, Days 4–5).**
   Configure ARIP for Customer's environment:
   - Custom `NormalizationConfig` mapping Customer's attribute
     names to ARIP canonical signals
   - Telemetry adapter for Customer's backend (if not already
     supported natively)
   - Integration with Customer's CI pipeline (`[GitHub Actions
     / GitLab CI / Jenkins / other]`)
   - Sticky comment configured on Customer's PR system

3. **Observation period (Week 2, Days 1–5).**
   Run ARIP in observe-mode against Customer's CI/staging
   telemetry for one week. Collect:
   - At minimum 3 real failure investigations
   - At minimum 1 weekly observation digest

4. **Findings + recommendation (Week 2, Day 5).**
   Written report covering:
   - What ARIP found, in plain English
   - Which of the 5 rules fired, with what confidence
   - Which abstention codes appeared, and what telemetry change
     would let those rules fire
   - **Honest GO / NO-GO recommendation** for production rollout
   - If GO: scope sketch for follow-on integration engagement
   - If NO-GO: specific reasons, what would change the recommendation

### 3. Deliverables

| # | Deliverable | Format | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Telemetry hygiene audit report | Markdown, ~10 pages | Day 3 |
| 2 | Working ARIP integration in Customer's CI | Code + config + 1 PR demonstrating sticky comment | Day 5 |
| 3 | One week of observation digests | Markdown, generated by `arip observe` | Day 10 |
| 4 | Per-failure investigation reports | Markdown, one per failure observed during pilot | Daily during Week 2 |
| 5 | Final findings + GO/NO-GO recommendation | Markdown, ~5 pages | Day 10 |

All deliverables are delivered electronically (Git repository,
email PDF, shared doc — Customer's choice).

### 4. Customer responsibilities

Customer will provide:

1. **By Day 1:**
   - Read-only access to telemetry backend (Jaeger UI URL or
     export of 1-hour sample; Loki/ES query access if applicable)
   - Repository access to `[CI pipeline configuration repository]`
   - Named engineering contact for technical questions
   - List of 2-3 recent CI failures Provider should specifically
     investigate during the pilot
2. **By Day 4:**
   - Approval of the proposed `NormalizationConfig`
   - Authorization to merge Provider's integration PR to CI
     configuration
3. **Ongoing during Week 2:**
   - Customer engineering contact responds to technical questions
     within 1 business day
   - Customer does not modify ARIP configuration during observation
     period (Provider will note any operational issues for the
     final report)

### 5. Out of scope

This pilot explicitly does NOT include:

- Modification of Customer's source code beyond CI configuration
- Production deployment of ARIP (separate engagement)
- Custom rule development beyond the 5 shipped rules
- Custom dashboard or web UI development (not a feature of ARIP)
- Integration with Customer's alerting / paging systems (ARIP
  is read-only by design)
- Performance benchmarking at scale (separate engagement)
- Training beyond the 1-hour handover session
- Ongoing support beyond the 30-day post-pilot bug-fix window

### 6. Pricing + payment terms

**Total fixed price: $`[5,000 — 10,000]`** plus expenses (capped at
$500, requires advance approval).

Payment schedule:

### 7. Timeline

| Phase | Days | Activity |
|---|---|---|
| Kickoff | Day 0 | SOW signed, kickoff call (30 min) |
| Audit | Days 1–3 | Telemetry hygiene audit + Deliverable 1 |
| Integration | Days 4–5 | CI integration + Deliverable 2 |
| Observation | Days 6–9 | Observe-mode running, Deliverables 3 and 4 |
| Findings | Day 10 | Deliverable 5 delivered, wrap-up call (1 hour) |

Total duration: 10 business days (~2 calendar weeks).

### 8. Acceptance criteria

Customer accepts the engagement if:

1. All 5 deliverables are delivered on or before the dates above
2. The deliverables are technically accurate (verifiable against
   Customer's telemetry)
3. The final report includes the GO/NO-GO recommendation with
   reasoning

Acceptance is communicated in writing within 5 business days of
Deliverable 5. Silence after 5 days = automatic acceptance.

If Customer disputes a deliverable, Provider has 5 business days
to remediate. If remediation is not possible, see Section 10.

### 9. Intellectual property

- **ARIP itself** (the open-source codebase) is governed by the
  Apache-2.0 license; this SOW does not modify those terms.
- **Customer-specific configuration** (NormalizationConfig YAML,
  CI workflow modifications, custom adapter code if developed)
  is delivered to Customer with no restrictions on use,
  modification, or further distribution.
- **Reports + deliverables** (audit, observation digests, findings)
  are Customer's property. Provider retains the right to reference
  the engagement existence (e.g., "I ran a pilot for a customer
  in [industry]") without disclosing Customer-identifying details
  unless Customer opts in to a public case study.
- **Aggregate, anonymized telemetry patterns** observed during
  the pilot may be incorporated into ARIP's calibration benchmark
  scenarios in non-identifying form, with Customer's written
  approval per pattern.

### 10. Refund policy

- If Provider fails to deliver any of the 5 deliverables by the
  dates in Section 7 (and remediation per Section 8 doesn't
  produce them): 50% refund of total fee.
- If Provider delivers all 5 but Customer chooses not to proceed
  with a follow-on engagement: no refund (Customer has the audit
  report and integration, both independently valuable).
- For Deliverable 1 (audit) specifically: full refund if the
  report contains demonstrable factual errors (i.e., claims
  about Customer's telemetry that are objectively false).
  "Disagreement on prioritization" does NOT qualify.

### 11. Confidentiality

Both parties agree:
- Customer's telemetry data, source code, and configuration are
  Customer's confidential information; Provider will not disclose.
- Engagement existence + general findings (in anonymized form)
  may be referenced by Provider unless Customer opts out.
- All deliverables may be shared by Customer internally without
  restriction.

This SOW does NOT supersede any separate NDA the parties have
signed.

### 12. Limitation of liability

Provider's total liability under this SOW is capped at the total
fee paid. Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential, or
punitive damages.

### 13. Governing law + dispute resolution

Governed by the laws of `[Customer's jurisdiction OR Provider's
jurisdiction — whichever is closer to Customer]`. Disputes
attempted to be resolved by direct discussion first; if
unresolved within 30 days, mediation in `[city]`.

## Operator notes (delete before sending)

**Negotiation hot-points:**
- Customers often push to add "training for the whole team" or
  "production deployment" to the scope — that's a separate
  engagement (Offering A). Hold the line.
- Customers may push to extend the observation period — fine, but
  re-scope and re-price.
- "Refund if we don't like it" — Section 10 covers this. Don't
  give blanket refunds.

**When to walk away:**
- Customer won't name an engineering contact
- Customer doesn't have distributed tracing AND isn't willing to
  add it
- Customer wants exclusivity or non-OSS terms
- Customer pushes back on the GO/NO-GO honesty (wants only GO
  scenarios)

**SOW size:** typical engagements have a 1-2 page SOW. This is
4-5 pages because the pilot is structured. If customer pushes
back on length, the negotiable sections are 9, 10, 12, 13.
Sections 1-8 are the actual scope.
